text:
maya: Ran a quick interleaved doc-order swap test on reranker-v2.
maya: Compared standard doc-order vs swapped-doc-order (docs reversed per query) across our 10k eval set.
maya: Observed avg NDCG@10 drop ~1.8%, MRR ~0.6% — curious if this is a formatting artifact or true relevance shift.
alex: Interesting. Do you mean you literally reversed the document list per query, keeping labels the same?
maya: yup. same relevance labels, just reversed the candidate order before scoring.
jordan: That can introduce caching/batch ordering effects in the runtime if there is any positional bias in the model or prefix cache.
lina: Also check tokenizer/truncation differences — if you append docs in order maybe the first doc gets more tokens and affects context.
maya: Good call. I inspected token lengths; distribution is similar but there's a small right-tail for swapped order.
alex: Can you paste the eval command you ran?
maya: Sure:

```
python eval_harness.py --model reranker-v2 --dataset prod-10k --split test --seed 42 --interleave swap_doc_order --metrics ndcg@10,mrr
```

maya: Eval-bot posted the summary:
eval-bot: NDGC@10: baseline 0.462 -> swapped 0.454 (-0.008), MRR baseline 0.329 -> swapped 0.327 (-0.002)
jordan: That -0.8% absolute on NDCG is non-trivial. What's the CI? Did you bootstrap or run multiple seeds?
maya: I only ran seed 42. CI unknown.
lina: Can we run a 5-seed bootstrap and also an interleaved-paired test? Pairwise tests reduce variance for per-query comparisons.
alex: Agreed. Also try randomizing doc order (not full reverse) to see if it's a reversal-specific effect.
maya: Plan: 1) 5 seeds (42,7,202,314,999), 2) random-shuffle-doc-order, 3) paired bootstrap (n=1000). I'll queue it on the cluster.
jordan: Add a run that disables KV-prefix caching on the serving side — to rule out runtime ordering effects. Flag: `--disable-kv-cache`.
maya: noted.

lina: Small note — when you shuffle docs, ensure the eval harness still maps preds to original doc ids for per-query metrics (no accidental rel label shuffle).
maya: Yup verified mapping intact.

alex: If effect persists across seeds and shuffle types, we should audit model granularity: are we using a cross-encoder that concatenates query+doc with doc position tokens? Maybe positional embeddings are leaking.
jordan: We should also test a quantized snapshot (int8) — quant can sometimes amplify small ranking noise.
maya: I'll include `--quantize int8` runs but run fewer seeds (2) to save cycles.

eval-bot: Queued runs: 5-seed paired-bootstrap, random-shuffle, disable-kv-cache, int8-smoke.
maya: ETA ~6 hours. Will post results.
alex: Thanks. If ndcg drop persists, let's prepare a minimal repro (single-query group) to send to model team.
lina: Thumbs up. Also add a metric slice by query length and doc length — might be concentrated in long-document queries.
maya: Added slice probes.

jordan: FYI, if you need a quick ci check, run `python -m scipy.stats.wilcoxon` on per-query diffs; paired nonparametric test.
maya: good tip.

alex: cool — ping when first results in.
maya: will do :smile:
